Data Encryption Standard

Purpose and scope

This standard sets out how Alderbridge encrypts data held on a laptop. It applies to every Alderbridge-issued laptop.

Policy statement

All Alderbridge laptops use full-disk encryption enabled by IT before issue, protecting resident and staff data if a laptop is lost or stolen.

Definitions

**Full-disk encryption** encryption applied to an entire device's storage, so data cannot be read without the correct credentials, even if the physical storage is removed. **Enabled before issue** the requirement that encryption is confirmed active before a laptop reaches its user, never enabled retrospectively after use has begun.

Enable full-disk encryption on every laptop before it is issued to a staff member.

Verify encryption status as part of IT's pre-issue checklist, never issuing a laptop where this check has not passed.

Report a laptop suspected to have been issued without encryption enabled to IT immediately for urgent remediation.

Include encryption verification in the annual device audit across all sites.

Interaction with other Alderbridge policies

This standard works alongside the Mobile Device Management Policy (governing the wider device management framework encryption sits within) and the Cyber Incident Response Plan (relevant where a lost device's encryption status affects the incident response).

Worked example

A worked example illustrates the value of pre-issue verification. A laptop is later reported lost by a staff member. Because IT's pre-issue checklist confirmed full-disk encryption was active before it was issued, the data on it remains protected, and this is confirmed and recorded as part of the lost-device response rather than being an open question at that stressful moment.

Frequently asked questions

**Can a staff member disable encryption on their own laptop for any reason?** No, this is technically restricted and never permitted regardless of the reason given. **What happens to an older laptop still in use that was issued before this standard was introduced?** IT verifies and enables encryption retrospectively as part of a rolling remediation programme.

Laundry Management Procedure

Purpose and scope

This procedure sets out how a resident's clothing and site linen is laundered at Alderbridge Care Group. It
applies to every site's laundry operation.

Policy statement

A resident's own clothing is laundered separately from site linen, clearly labelled, and washed at a
temperature appropriate to the fabric, while soiled linen follows a specific infection-control hot-wash
standard.

Definitions

**Resident's own clothing** clothing belonging to and worn by an individual resident, laundered separately
and returned to them. **Site linen** bedding, towels and similar items not tied to a specific resident.
**Soiled linen** linen contaminated with a bodily fluid, requiring the infection-control hot-wash standard.

Roles and responsibilities

**Laundry staff** launder a resident's clothing separately, labelled, and follow the correct wash
temperature for the item type. **Care staff** identify and bag soiled linen correctly for separate handling.
**The registered manager** ensures the laundry operation meets this procedure's standard.

1. Label every resident's clothing clearly on admission, and again promptly if a label is lost or becomes
illegible.

2. Launder a resident's own clothing separately from another resident's items and from site linen, at a
temperature appropriate to the fabric.

3. Wash soiled linen at 60 degrees Celsius, following the infection-control hot-wash standard, handled
separately from the point of collection.

4. Return laundered clothing to the correct resident promptly, checking labelling at the point of return.

5. Report a persistent labelling or mix-up issue to the registered manager for investigation.

Exceptions and professional judgement

Where a specific fabric or garment cannot tolerate the standard wash temperature (for example, a delicate
item), laundry staff use the manufacturer's care label instructions instead, recording the exception so it is
not treated as an error at the next audit.

Purpose and scope

This procedure sets out how Alderbridge Care Group responds to a reference request for a current or
former staff member. It applies to every reference request received by HR.

Policy statement

HR provides a factual reference confirming dates of employment and job title within 5 working days of a
request, tightened from the previous 10 working days, giving a former or current staff member a faster,
reliable response supporting their next step.

Definitions

**Factual reference** a reference limited to objective facts such as dates of employment and job title, as
distinct from a subjective opinion-based reference. **Reference request** a request received in writing
from a prospective employer or other authorised party, with the staff member's consent where required.

Roles and responsibilities

**HR** processes every reference request and issues the factual reference within the tightened
5-working-day timeframe. **The staff member's line manager** is not the point of contact for a formal
reference request, which is handled centrally by HR to ensure consistency. **The requesting party**
provides sufficient detail, including the staff member's consent where required, for HR to process the
request.

1. Log every reference request on receipt, confirming it includes sufficient detail and any required consent.

2. Issue a factual reference confirming dates of employment and job title within 5 working days of the
request being received, a tightening from the previous 10-working-day standard.

3. Limit the reference to factual, objective information; a subjective opinion on the staff member's
performance or conduct is not included.

4. Direct a request for a fuller, opinion-based reference to the registered manager, who decides whether
and how to respond to that specific, different type of request.

Post-incident review process

Following any Tier 2 or higher incident, IT leads a post-incident review within 10 working days of resolution, documenting what worked, what did not, and any change needed to this plan, the severity model, or a specific system's own resilience.

Detailed containment procedure by system type

Containment differs meaningfully depending on the affected system's nature. For a single endpoint device (a laptop, tablet or desktop), IT disconnects it from the network immediately, either physically or via remote network access revocation, without powering it off, since powering off can destroy volatile memory evidence useful to a later forensic review. For a server-based system, IT isolates the affected server segment at the network switch level rather than the individual server, since a compromised server may have already spread laterally to a degree not yet visible. For a cloud-hosted system, IT contacts the cloud provider's own security team in parallel with internal containment, since a cloud environment's containment options differ from an on-premises one and often require provider-side action IT cannot take unilaterally.

Detailed containment procedure by system type (continued)

For a network device itself (a router, switch or firewall), IT does not simply power-cycle it, since this can both destroy evidence and, in some compromise scenarios, trigger a malicious payload configured to activate on restart; instead, a specialist is engaged to assess before any restart is attempted. For a shared care records system spanning multiple sites, IT considers whether a partial, site-by-site isolation is sufficient rather than isolating the entire system nationally, weighing the containment benefit against the operational disruption a full isolation would cause to sites with no evidence of compromise.

Evidence preservation

Before any remediation step that could alter or destroy evidence, IT takes a forensic image or detailed log export of the affected system where practicable, since a later insurance claim, regulatory enquiry, or law enforcement investigation may depend on evidence that a hurried remediation step could otherwise destroy. This preservation step does not delay an urgent containment action itself, but is completed as soon as the immediate containment is achieved and before full remediation begins.

Recognising burnout specifically

Beyond general wellbeing, managers are trained to recognise the specific signs of burnout common in care work — persistent exhaustion not resolved by rest, growing cynicism or detachment from a role someone previously enjoyed, and a sense of reduced personal effectiveness — since burnout often develops gradually and is easy to mistake for an ordinary bad patch until it has become genuinely serious, and early, proactive conversation makes a real difference to how well and how quickly someone recovers.

Peer support and team-level wellbeing

Beyond individual support routes, registered managers are encouraged to build genuine peer support into team culture — protected time to debrief after a difficult shift, and normalising open conversation about the emotional demands of care work — recognising that a team culture where struggling is treated as shameful undermines every individual support route this guidance otherwise provides.

Phishing as the most common entry point

The large majority of cyber incidents Alderbridge has investigated began with a phishing email, a message crafted to look legitimate that persuades a staff member to click a malicious link, open an infected attachment, or enter their credentials on a fraudulent page. Recognising a phishing attempt is therefore the single most valuable skill in preventing an incident before it begins, and this plan's own effectiveness depends heavily on the wider phishing awareness training staff complete annually, since a fast response to an incident already underway is always a worse outcome than the incident never starting.

Common phishing indicators staff are trained to notice

Indicator	Why it matters
Urgent or threatening language demanding immediate action	Designed to bypass a staff member's normal caution
A sender address that looks almost, but not quite, right	A common technique to impersonate a trusted colleague or supplier
A link that, when hovered over, shows a different address than the text displayed	Reveals the link's true destination before it is clicked
A request to enter a password on an unfamiliar page	Legitimate systems rarely ask for a password via an emailed link
An unexpected attachment, especially one requiring a security setting to be changed to open	A common technique to bypass built-in file safety checks

What to do with a suspected phishing email

A staff member who receives a suspected phishing email does not click any link or open any attachment, forwards it to the IT service desk using the reporting function built into the email system, and then deletes it. If a link has already been clicked or an attachment already opened, this is reported to IT immediately rather than being kept quiet out of embarrassment, since a prompt report is what allows fast containment, and delaying a report solely to avoid an awkward conversation is exactly the kind of decision that turns a contained Tier 1 incident into a wider one.

Purpose and scope

This procedure sets out how Alderbridge Care Group manages a confirmed asbestos register at a site where one applies. It currently applies to Riverside House and Moorland View only, the two older North West buildings with a confirmed asbestos register.

Policy statement

Definitions

Data protection impact assessments

A data protection impact assessment (DPIA) is completed before Alderbridge introduces any new
technology or process likely to result in a high risk to individuals' rights and freedoms — for example, a
new type of monitoring sensor in a resident's room, or a new AI-assisted rostering tool that processes staff
personal data in a novel way. The DPIA is led by the Data Protection Lead, involves genuine consultation
with the people supported or staff who would be affected wherever practicable rather than being
completed as a desk exercise alone, and its outcome — including any mitigation adopted or, in a small
number of cases, a decision not to proceed with the proposal at all — is recorded and retained as
evidence that the risk was actually considered before roll-out, not afterward.

Relationship with consent-based marketing

Where Alderbridge occasionally sends a newsletter or event invitation to family members who have opted
in, that processing is kept entirely separate from care-related communication: consent is recorded
specifically for the marketing purpose, can be withdrawn at any time through a clearly signposted method
in every communication sent, and withdrawing that consent never affects, or is ever perceived to affect,
the standard of care a resident receives — a boundary Alderbridge treats as absolute precisely because of
the vulnerability of the relationship involved.

Third-party requests for information

A request for personal data from a party other than the data subject themselves — a solicitor, an insurer,
the police, or another care provider a resident is transferring to — is never actioned on the strength of the
request alone. The Data Protection Lead confirms the requester's legal basis and identity first, and where
the request comes from the police, confirms whether it is made under a specific statutory
information-sharing power before any data is released, recording that confirmation in writing regardless of
how routine or urgent the request appears to be, since urgency is never itself a substitute for lawful basis.

Key safe codes

Community support workers across the Midlands Region (not only Willow Bank, as in the prior version) record each client's key safe code in the secure app, never on paper, and report any code change to the office within 24 hours.

Authorisation and coding

A key safe is installed only after property-owner consent, resident or representative agreement where applicable, and a recorded risk assessment. The code is disclosed only to authorised workers who need access and is not written in general notes, visit lists or an unprotected message. Each safe has a unique register entry linked to the address without exposing the code itself.

Use and security

Staff shield the keypad, return the key immediately, scramble the display and confirm the safe has locked before leaving. A missing key, damaged safe, observed code or unexplained access is reported immediately and the premises secured through the agreed contingency route. The code is changed after compromise and at other defined review points.

Review and removal

The responsible manager reviews continuing need, authorised recipients and physical condition at least annually and after a tenancy, care-package or risk change. When the safe is no longer required it is removed or disabled promptly, keys are returned and access records are closed. Installation, code-change, incident, review and removal evidence is retained securely.

On-Call Manager Procedure

Purpose and scope

This procedure sets out how staff contact an on-call manager outside of normal hours for a care-related concern requiring senior management input. It applies to every site.

Policy statement

Out of hours, staff call the single central on-call mobile number, answered on a weekly rota by one of four senior managers, providing a single, reliable route to senior management support at any hour.

Definitions

**On-call manager** the senior manager currently holding the weekly on-call rota responsibility. **Central on-call number** the single mobile number every site calls, regardless of region, to reach the current on-call manager. **Weekly rota** the rotation among four senior managers, each taking on-call responsibility for one week at a time.

Roles and responsibilities

**Any staff member** on shift calls the central on-call number for a genuine out-of-hours concern requiring senior management input. **The on-call manager** answers the central number during their rota week and provides guidance or attends site as the situation requires. **HR** maintains the weekly rota and ensures every senior manager knows their upcoming on-call weeks well in advance.

Call the single central on-call mobile number for any out-of-hours concern requiring senior management input, regardless of which site or region is calling.

Give a clear, concise account of the situation to the on-call manager who answers, including what has already been done.

Follow the on-call manager's guidance, or arrange for them to attend site if they judge this necessary.

Record the call and its outcome in the site's on-call log.

Safer Recruitment: Manager Guidance Notes

Purpose and scope

These guidance notes support every hiring manager at Alderbridge Care Group in recruiting safely, fairly and consistently, expanding on the Recruitment and Selection Policy's own overarching standard with the practical detail a hiring manager needs at each stage of the process. They apply to every recruitment for a role with any level of contact with people supported, and in modified form to every other Alderbridge role.

Policy statement

Safer recruitment is not a single check completed once at the end of a hiring process; it is a discipline applied at every stage, from how a job is advertised through to a new starter's supervised first weeks, because the people Alderbridge supports are often less able than most to protect themselves if a genuinely unsuitable person is ever recruited into a caring role.

Definitions

**Enhanced DBS check** the highest level of criminal record check available for a role involving regulated activity with adults, required before an unsupervised start in a care-facing role. **DBS Update Service** an optional service allowing faster verification of an existing DBS certificate's continued validity between full rechecks. **Regulated activity** the specific category of work with adults at risk that legally requires an enhanced DBS check. **Interim risk assessment** a documented, time-limited arrangement allowing a supervised start pending a DBS certificate, used only where the registered manager has assessed it as genuinely safe to do so.

Roles and responsibilities

**The hiring manager** leads shortlisting, interviewing and reference requests for their own vacancy. **HR** verifies every check (DBS, references, right to work) is genuinely completed before confirming a start date, and holds the master safer recruitment checklist for every hire. **At least one interview panel member** has completed safer recruitment training within the last 3 years, per the wider Recruitment and Selection Policy. **The registered manager** authorises, and takes personal responsibility for, any interim risk assessment permitting a supervised start pending DBS.

Cyber Incident Response Plan

Purpose and scope

This plan sets out how Alderbridge Care Group responds to a suspected cyber security incident, including ransomware, a data breach, or unauthorised system access. It applies to every site and every system holding Alderbridge or resident data.

Policy statement

A cyber incident is contained, reported and recovered from quickly and in a coordinated way, minimising harm to resident data and the continuity of care systems staff depend on.

Definitions

**Cyber incident** any suspected compromise of an Alderbridge system, including ransomware, phishing-derived compromise, or unauthorised access. **Containment** the immediate step of isolating an affected system to prevent further spread. **The Data Protection Officer** the role responsible for assessing whether an incident also constitutes a personal data breach requiring ICO notification.

Roles and responsibilities

**Any member of staff** who suspects a cyber incident reports it to IT immediately, without attempting to investigate or fix it themselves. **IT** contains the affected system, begins investigation, and engages external specialist support where needed. **The Data Protection Officer** assesses the data breach implications in parallel with IT's technical response.

Report a suspected cyber incident to IT immediately, including a suspicious email already clicked, an unusual system prompt, or a system behaving unexpectedly.

IT isolates the affected device or system from the network immediately on receiving a report, prioritising containment over initial diagnosis.

Do not pay a ransomware demand, and do not negotiate with an attacker; this decision sits with the Chief Executive in consultation with external specialist advice, never with an individual site.

The Data Protection Officer assesses within 24 hours whether the incident constitutes a personal data breach requiring notification to the ICO within the statutory 72-hour window.

Restore affected systems from a verified clean backup only once IT confirms the original vulnerability has been addressed, not simply restoring and reconnecting immediately.

Data Protection Policy

Purpose and scope

This policy sets out how Alderbridge Care Group meets its obligations under the UK GDPR and Data
Protection Act 2018 when processing personal data about people supported, staff, job applicants, and
anyone else whose data Alderbridge holds. It applies to every site, every system, and every format
personal data is held in, whether digital, paper, photographic or verbal, and to every member of staff,
volunteer, contractor and agency worker with any access to it.

Policy statement

Alderbridge treats personal data, and in particular the special category health and care data it holds about
people supported, as something staff are trusted with rather than something they are simply permitted to
use. A breach of this policy is taken as seriously as a breach of any safeguarding or medication standard,
because a data breach involving a vulnerable person's health information can itself cause real, lasting
harm.

Definitions

**Personal data** any information relating to an identified or identifiable living person. **Special category
data** personal data revealing health, ethnicity, religion, sexual orientation or similar, subject to stricter
conditions for processing. **Data controller** the organisation (Alderbridge) that decides why and how
personal data is processed. **Data processor** a third party (for example, a payroll provider) processing
personal data on Alderbridge's behalf under a contract. **Lawful basis** the specific legal ground under
UK GDPR Article 6 (and, for special category data, Article 9) that justifies a particular processing activity.
**Data subject** the individual the personal data is about.

Medication Fridge Breakdown Procedure

*Supersedes the version effective 1 April 2025. Escalation changed to also require a call to the supplying pharmacy, not only the on-call manager.*

If the fridge fails

Keep the affected fridge closed, do not move stock on assumption, and call both the on-call manager and the supplying pharmacy (a new requirement — the previous version only required the on-call manager) for advice on whether the stock remains usable; see Immediate containment below for the full response, including when a validated alternative storage location may be used.

Immediate containment

When the medicines-fridge temperature is outside range or the unit fails, staff keep the door closed, note the current and available minimum/maximum readings, label the unit not for use and inform the responsible nurse or manager. Stock is not moved into a domestic refrigerator or discarded on assumption. A validated alternative refrigerator or insulated container is prepared where authorised.

Clinical and pharmacy advice

Staff list every affected medicine, batch where available, storage requirement and estimated exposure time and obtain product-specific pharmacy or manufacturer advice. The decision to use, quarantine or replace each item is recorded. Time-critical doses are escalated so an alternative supply or clinically appropriate plan can be arranged without bypassing prescribing controls.

Recovery and assurance

The failed unit is inspected and must demonstrate a stable compliant temperature before return to service. Quarantined stock remains segregated until a documented decision is made. Temperature records, exposure assessment, advice, stock disposition, engineer report and any omitted-dose or incident record are retained together, and repeated failures trigger equipment replacement review.

Purpose and scope

This policy sets out how annual leave is calculated, requested and approved across Alderbridge Care
Group, including the leave year, carry-over rules, and notice periods for requesting leave. It applies to

Policy statement

Rest and recovery time is treated as essential to sustaining good care over the long term, not a
discretionary benefit; this policy is designed to make leave genuinely straightforward to request and take,
while being honest about the real staffing constraints a 24-hour care environment operates under.

Definitions

**Leave year** the 12-month period, 1 April to 31 March, against which annual leave entitlement and
usage is measured. **Pro-rata entitlement** the proportionally reduced entitlement calculated for a
part-time employee based on their contracted hours relative to full-time. **Carried-over leave** unused
leave from one leave year moved into the next under the specific conditions this policy allows. **Peak
period** the Christmas and New Year period, during which a longer notice period applies to leave requests
given typically higher demand.

Roles and responsibilities

**The employee** submits leave requests via the rota system within the notice periods this policy sets out.
**The registered manager** approves or declines requests, balancing fair access to leave against
maintaining safe staffing levels, and communicates a decision within a reasonable time so employees can
plan. **HR** tracks entitlement and carry-over centrally and advises on any complex calculation (for
example, for an employee who changed hours partway through the leave year).

Extended frequently asked questions

**If I'm off sick, do I still accrue annual leave?** Yes — annual leave continues to accrue during any period of sickness absence, in the same way as during active employment. **What if I disagree with occupational health's assessment of my fitness to return?** Discuss this with HR, who can arrange a further opinion or explore a modified return plan; the assessment informs the decision but is not applied rigidly without regard to your own account of how you are actually feeling. **Is there a limit to how much company sick pay I can receive in a year?** Yes, set out in your contract of employment and varying by length of service; once company sick pay is exhausted, statutory sick pay continues for as long as you remain eligible under current legislation. **Can I be asked to attend a return-to-work discussion by phone if I'm still recovering?** The discussion is normally held in person on your first day back, but where genuinely necessary can be arranged differently; the purpose (support, not box-ticking) matters more than the specific format.

How trigger points are calculated in practice

HR calculates trigger points using a rolling 12-month window measured backward from the most recent absence, not a fixed calendar year, so that an occasion from 13 months ago naturally drops out of the calculation without needing to be manually excluded, and every occasion within the current rolling window counts regardless of whether it happened at the very start or the very end of that window; this rolling approach is explained to every employee at induction, since a fixed calendar-year approach would otherwise create an artificial reset each January that does not reflect the underlying pattern being monitored.

Backup strategy underpinning recovery

Alderbridge's backup strategy follows the widely recognised 3-2-1 principle: at least three copies of critical data, stored on two different types of media, with at least one copy held off-site or in a separate cloud region from the primary system. This structure is what makes the 'restore from a verified clean backup' step in this plan realistic rather than aspirational, since a single, co-located backup can be compromised by the same incident that affected the primary system it was meant to protect against.

Backup testing and verification

A backup is only useful if it can genuinely be restored when needed, so IT performs a scheduled test restoration of a sample backup on a regular cycle, confirming both that the backup file itself is intact and that the restoration process actually produces a working system, rather than discovering a backup was corrupted or incomplete only at the point of a genuine incident when there is no time left to find out.

Third-party and supplier risk

A cyber incident does not always originate within an Alderbridge-controlled system; a supplier or third-party provider with its own access to Alderbridge data or systems represents a genuine risk if that supplier's own security is weaker than Alderbridge's own standard. Before granting a supplier system access, IT assesses the supplier's own security practice at a level proportionate to the access being granted, and a supplier holding significant access is required to notify Alderbridge promptly of any security incident on their own side that could affect Alderbridge data.

Where a supplier notifies Alderbridge of an incident on their own side, or where Alderbridge's own investigation traces an incident's origin to a supplier system, IT treats this with the same urgency as an internally-originating incident, applying the same severity tier classification and engaging the supplier's own incident response team as part of the coordinated response.

Auditing the suite as a whole

Beyond auditing each specific procedure on its own terms, the organisation-level Safeguarding Lead conducts an annual whole-suite audit, sampling a cross-section of cases across every specific safeguarding procedure to confirm the suite functions coherently for a situation genuinely spanning several of its specific procedures at once.

Confidentiality and information governance in a safeguarding case

Safeguarding information is held to the same confidentiality standard as any other resident record, accessed only by those with a genuine need to know as part of their role in the specific case, and never discussed informally outside that circle; this confidentiality standard sits alongside, and is never used to avoid, the duty to escalate and share information appropriately within the safeguarding process itself, including under the multi-agency information sharing appendix.

Handling an anonymous safeguarding concern

A concern raised anonymously, whether through the Whistleblowing Policy's own anonymous route or otherwise, is investigated with the same seriousness as a concern raised openly, since the value of the information itself does not depend on who raised it; this applies equally to an anonymous concern about self-neglect raised by, for example, a worried neighbour or visitor.

Reviewing this overarching policy's own effectiveness

Beyond the specific procedure reviews and the whole-suite audit, the Board periodically considers whether the safeguarding framework as a whole, including this overarching document's own structure, remains fit for purpose, informed by external benchmarking against sector guidance and any relevant regulatory feedback.

Preventing self-neglect through early identification

Regular, attentive contact with a resident is itself a preventive measure against self-neglect reaching a serious point unnoticed; staff are trained to notice a gradual change in a resident's self-care, mood, or engagement with their environment as early as possible, since intervening supportively at an early stage is both kinder to the resident and more effective than responding only once the situation has become significantly more serious.

Medication Fridge Monitoring: Daily Checks

Purpose and scope

This guidance sets out how the medication fridge is monitored at every Alderbridge site. It applies to every shift storing medication requiring refrigeration.

Policy statement

The medication fridge is checked and logged daily, keeping medication within its required temperature range so that it remains safe and effective for resident use.

Definitions

**Acceptable range** 2 to 8 degrees Celsius, the temperature band medication stored in the fridge must remain within. **Fridge log** the daily record of the fridge's temperature, checked and signed each day. **Out-of-range reading** any reading outside the acceptable range, requiring immediate action.

1. Check and record the fridge temperature once daily, at a consistent time, in the fridge log.
2. Where a reading is out of range, recheck immediately; if confirmed, follow the Medication Fridge Breakdown Procedure without delay.
3. Keep the fridge door closed as much as practicable, avoiding unnecessary or prolonged opening.
4. Report a fridge showing a recurring near-boundary reading to facilities, even if it has not yet gone fully out of range.

Interaction with other Alderbridge policies

A worked example illustrates the daily check in practice. The morning shift lead checks the fridge temperature at the same time each day as part of their routine, records 4 degrees in the log, and moves on; a fortnight later, a reading of 9 degrees prompts an immediate recheck and, once confirmed, the breakdown procedure is followed straight away rather than waiting to see if it corrects itself.

Safeguarding Training Levels: Who Needs What

Purpose and scope

This guidance explains the different levels of safeguarding training required across Alderbridge roles. It applies to every member of staff and every registered manager.

Policy statement

Safeguarding training is matched to a role's actual level of resident contact and responsibility, so that every staff member holds the depth of training genuinely relevant to their duties.

Definitions

**Level 1** basic safeguarding awareness, required for every member of staff regardless of role. **Level 2** intermediate training for a role with direct, regular resident contact. **Level 3** advanced training for a registered manager, deputy, or designated Safeguarding Champion.

1. Complete Level 1 safeguarding awareness training as part of induction, regardless of role.
2. Complete Level 2 training within the first month for any role involving direct, regular resident contact.
3. Complete Level 3 training before taking on a registered manager, deputy, or Safeguarding Champion role.
4. Refresh the applicable level every three years, or sooner if guidance changes significantly.

How the suite is kept up to date

A specific safeguarding procedure is reviewed on its own cycle, but any change is also checked against this overarching document and its appendix to confirm consistency across the whole suite.

Introducing a new specific safeguarding procedure

Where a genuinely new type of safeguarding concern emerges that the current suite does not clearly cover, the Safeguarding Lead drafts a new specific procedure following the same core principles this overarching document sets out.

Recognising a financial concern in practice

A financial concern does not always present as an obvious theft; staff are trained to notice a subtler pattern such as a resident's belongings or money disappearing gradually, a family member's sudden, unexplained interest in a resident's finances, or a resident expressing confusion or distress about their own money that is out of character for their usual level of understanding. Any such pattern is escalated in the same way as a more obvious concern, since financial abuse is often gradual rather than a single dramatic event.

Coordinating a financial concern with the Finance function

While the Safeguarding Lead now receives the initial escalation directly, the Finance function remains closely involved in reviewing the underlying financial records once a concern has been raised, since the safeguarding response and the financial audit trail review are complementary, not competing, parts of a full investigation.

Safeguarding Adults Board engagement

Alderbridge participates in the relevant local authority's Safeguarding Adults Board where a site's residents fall within that authority's area, contributing to multi-agency learning and receiving updates on local safeguarding priorities; the Safeguarding Lead represents Alderbridge at this Board and cascades relevant learning back into the safeguarding suite and staff training.

The role of an advocate

Where a resident lacks capacity to fully participate in a safeguarding process, or would benefit from independent support regardless of capacity, an independent advocate is arranged to represent the resident's own wishes and interests throughout the process, distinct from a family member's role, since a family member, however well-intentioned, may have their own perspective that does not always align precisely with the resident's own wishes.

Policy statement

A resident's money is handled with the same care and transparency Alderbridge would expect if it were its

record aspect once a concern is raised. **Care staff** record every transaction involving a resident's
personal allowance at the time it occurs, never relying on memory to reconstruct it later.

Retention

Mailboxes are retained for 6 months after an employee leaves (shortened from the previous 2-year
period), then permanently deleted.

Classification and filing

Email is a communication channel, not an indefinite records store. A message evidencing a care,
employment, contractual, complaint, safeguarding or governance decision is transferred promptly to the
approved record system and classified under the applicable retention schedule. Routine coordination,
duplicates, alerts and transient working messages are deleted when no longer needed.

Retention and disposal

Mailbox retention settings support, but do not replace, the duty to file a business record correctly.
Automatic deletion is suspended for a legal hold, investigation, subject-access search or other authorised
preservation requirement. When the hold ends, disposal resumes under the relevant schedule and is
recorded where the record class requires evidence of destruction.

Access and assurance

Managers arrange controlled mailbox access for absence, leavers or investigations through the
documented authorisation route; passwords are never shared. Information Governance reviews retention
configuration, preservation holds and exception reports at least annually. Staff report misdirected sensitive
email immediately under the Data Breach Procedure rather than attempting to resolve it silently.

Communicating with residents and families during a cyber incident

Where a cyber incident genuinely affects a resident-facing system or resident data, the registered manager at an affected site is briefed by IT and, working with the Communications function, provides residents and families with a clear, honest, appropriately reassuring update, avoiding both alarming over-disclosure of technical detail and an unhelpfully vague reassurance that understates a genuine concern. Working with external specialist support

At Tier 3 or above, IT engages Alderbridge's retained external cyber security specialist firm, whose contact details and engagement terms are held centrally by IT and the cyber insurance provider. This external specialist provides forensic investigation capacity and negotiation expertise beyond what Alderbridge's internal IT team can reasonably be expected to hold in-house, given that a serious cyber incident is a rare but high-consequence event.

Recovery testing before full restoration

Before a restored system is returned to full production use, IT completes a defined set of recovery tests confirming both that the vulnerability has genuinely been addressed and that the restored system functions correctly, rather than declaring recovery complete based on the backup restoration alone succeeding technically. A system is returned to a limited, monitored production state first, with full unrestricted use following only once this monitored period confirms no recurrence.

Missing Person Procedure

Supersedes the version effective 1 July 2024. Immediate-search window shortened from 30 to 15 minutes.

1. Immediate search

A 15-minute site and immediate-grounds search is conducted (shortened from the previous 30 minutes)
before escalating further.

2. Police contact

If not found after the immediate search, police are called on 101 (or 999 if there is immediate risk).

Immediate response

Staff confirm the person is not elsewhere on site, note the last verified sighting, clothing, mobility,
communication needs and likely destinations, and preserve relevant CCTV or access records. The
registered manager assesses immediate vulnerability and calls emergency services without delay where
risk is high; local searching never postpones a necessary police report.

Search and communication

The search is coordinated, logged and allocated so unsafe duplication and unsearched areas are visible.
Staff maintain safe staffing for residents who remain on site. Family, commissioners and safeguarding
contacts are informed according to the person's plan and the circumstances, while public communication
and photographs are released only through the police-led or otherwise authorised route.

Return and learning

On return, immediate welfare and medical needs are assessed before a calm account is sought. The care
plan, risk assessment and known triggers are reviewed with the person and relevant representatives. The
incident record includes timings, decisions, notifications and search activity, and repeated episodes or
control failures are escalated for safeguarding and service-level review.
